title: MoonLamp
subtitle: A 3D-printed moon that shows the real lunar phase

maturity.label: Built; firmware running on the lamp

pitch: A 3D-printed moon with hand-designed, hand-soldered electronics on an ESP32, lit by a WS2811 strip and kept on time by a real-time clock.
highlights: Hand-designed and hand-soldered the electronics on an ESP32
5 V WS2811 strip, with a PCF8523 real-time clock on I2C and a coin-cell backup
Firmware running on the lamp: true lunar phase, earthshine, blue moons, and eclipses

blocks.md: MoonLamp is a personal build: a 3D-printed moon that lights itself to match the real Moon. I designed and 3D-printed the shell and hand-designed and hand-soldered the electronics: an ESP32 driving a 5 V WS2811 strip, with a PCF8523 real-time clock on I2C and a coin-cell backup.

The firmware (C/C++ in the Arduino IDE), which I reworked, integrated, and debugged, runs on the lamp and renders the true lunar phase, earthshine, blue moons, and eclipses. The first run was steady, with no flicker.
Next: the documentation and the code in the project's GitHub repository.
